claims.text: The selected alloy has nominal composition AlNbTiVZr0.25.
The initial alloy is as-cast, arc-melted, and homogenized.
The homogenized alloy has a nearly random distribution of its constituent elements.
No superconductivity has been observed in the initial alloy at low temperature.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce short-range chemical order through subtle atomic rearrangements without causing phase segregation.
Annealing-induced local chemical order produces nanoscale compositional fluctuations.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations modify the electronic density of states.
Atomic-scale chemical ordering enhances the density of electronic states near the Fermi level.
The enhanced density of states increases local electron-phonon coupling.
Increased local electron-phonon coupling fosters Cooper-pair formation in chemically ordered regions.
Superconducting ordered regions can form a percolative superconducting path across the sample.
Annealed samples with induced chemical ordering will have a higher superconducting critical temperature than the homogenized baseline.
Annealed samples with induced chemical ordering will have a greater superconducting volume fraction than the homogenized baseline.
Superconductivity in the homogenized baseline is absent or significantly suppressed.
The homogenized baseline lacks enough localized chemical order to support the robust electron-phonon coupling required for superconductivity.
The proposed effect should extend to refractory high-entropy alloys having similar amounts of chemical disorder.
Annealing-induced phase separation may limit the proposed ordering effect.
Very high intrinsic disorder may prevent effective local ordering and thereby limit the proposed effect.
